    STADL palette as a plotly colorscale

    stadl_colorscale.Rd

    STADL palette as a plotly colorscale

    stadl_colorscale(palette = "raspberry_turquoise", n = 11, reverse = FALSE)

    Arguments

    palette

    Name of a palette, see stadl_palette_names().

    n

    Number of color stops. Default 11.

    reverse

    Logical. Reverse the order of the colors?

    Value

    A list of list(position, hex) pairs with positions from 0 to 1, as expected by the colorscale attribute of plotly traces.

    Examples

    stadl_colorscale("turquoise", n = 5)
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]][[1]]
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> [[1]][[2]]
#> [1] "#F1F9F9"
#> 
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [[2]][[1]]
#> [1] 0.25
#> 
#> [[2]][[2]]
#> [1] "#B1DDE0"
#> 
#> 
#> [[3]]
#> [[3]][[1]]
#> [1] 0.5
#> 
#> [[3]][[2]]
#> [1] "#61BFC5"
#> 
#> 
#> [[4]]
#> [[4]][[1]]
#> [1] 0.75
#> 
#> [[4]][[2]]
#> [1] "#338C93"
#> 
#> 
#> [[5]]
#> [[5]][[1]]
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> [[5]][[2]]
#> [1] "#274143"
#> 
#> 

if (requireNamespace("plotly", quietly = TRUE)) {
  # heatmap with a sequential colorscale
  plotly::plot_ly(z = volcano, type = "heatmap",
                  colorscale = stadl_colorscale("raspberry"))

  # discrete colors
  plotly::plot_ly(iris, x = ~Sepal.Width, y = ~Sepal.Length,
                  color = ~Species, colors = stadl_colors(),
                  type = "scatter", mode = "markers")

  # continuous color mapping
  plotly::plot_ly(iris, x = ~Sepal.Width, y = ~Sepal.Length,
                  color = ~Petal.Length, colors = stadl_pal("turquoise"),
                  type = "scatter", mode = "markers")
}
